correctness.rationale: The disjoint odd-indexed cycle parity forts give the sharp lower bound of one seed per cycle; deleting any putative size-k seed leaves a tree with even arms attached to its ports. A perfect matching of the residual tree must match every port along a bridge, and conversely a perfect bridge-tree matching extends to the residual tree by internally matching even arms. Empty-set skew forcing of a forest is equivalent to a perfect matching by the one-force-per-vertex permutation argument and matched-leaf induction. This gives both necessity and sufficiency for every tree and every even cycle length. Independent exhaustive programs from actual final artifact paths agree on six finite cases, including no-perfect-matching examples, and verify exact exchange and slide edges. Unproved: exact optimum when the bridge tree lacks a matching; any more general cactus geometry.

value.rationale: Gives an exact, all-parameters structural classification and a sharp existence threshold governed by a nonlocal perfect matching in the interblock tree. This realizes every even-factor Hamming graph as a minimum skew-forcing exchange graph on a connected cactus, while proving complete token-slide immobility. Such precise distinctions between connected-source global reachability and locally constrained motion are natural reconfiguration questions and are not consequences of merely computing Z^- on a single graph.
